label: Person
name: Henry Hubbard
summary:
Henry Hubbard (1784–1857) was an American Democratic politician from New Hampshire who served as U.S. Representative (1817–1829), U.S. Senator (1835–1841), and Governor of New Hampshire (1841–1843). His combined congressional and gubernatorial career spanned the Era of Good Feelings through the heart of the Jacksonian period — nearly three decades of major office-holding. New Hampshire's reliably Democratic politics and Hubbard's alignment with the Jackson coalition gave him sustained electoral success through multiple state and federal offices. His Senate years covered the Bank War's final stages and the Van Buren administration.

He was a Charlestown New Hampshire lawyer who represented the Connecticut River valley's Democratic communities.

He held more years of combined major office than almost any other New Hampshire antebellum politician.

He was New Hampshire's most experienced early Jacksonian Democrat.
